page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m2.large is an entry-tier virtual server configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 4.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The compute layer is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, virtualized through KVM. The 2 vCPUs are assigned from a single physical execution core using hyperthreading. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting extended instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage and no GPU hardware accelerators, relying on remote block storage for file systems. Baseline network capacity is rated at 1 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses allocated.

Benchmark results categorize the instance within the lower percentiles across compute, memory, and throughput metrics. Single-core compute evaluations yield a Geekbench score of 919.0 and a stress-ng score of 1093.88. Multi-core performance reflects the limits of a single physical core, scoring 1093.0 in Geekbench and 1458.47 in stress-ng. Memory bandwidth benchmarks record 9.92 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 9.22 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, the server handled 1.47 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved 1.26 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its minimal resource footprint, the server delivers an economical profile for workloads with modest computational demands. The lack of onboard storage and modest CPU throughput make it unsuitable for high-throughput databases, parallel batch processing, or machine learning workloads. It is functionally aligned with lightweight utility tasks, development and staging nodes, small microservices, and low-traffic web hosting.
